# OpenAuth

> OpenAuth is a database-agnostic authentication toolkit for Node.js. It provides email OTP verification, JWT access and refresh sessions with rotation and reuse detection, and per-flow lockouts, behind one core API that never touches your database driver directly.

OpenAuth solves repeat auth plumbing: instead of rewriting login for every database, one core adapts to the schema you already run through adapters.

- Backend and library source: https://github.com/abdrahman-dev/openauth
- This documentation site source: https://github.com/abdrahman-dev/openauth-site
- Maintainer: Abdrahman Mussa

## Main concepts

- **Core**: all auth decisions live in one database-agnostic core (`createAuth`), shared by any consumer of the library.
- **Adapters**: the only bridge between core and database. User operations plus session operations, normalized to `UserRecord` / `SessionRecord` shapes.
- **Sessions**: short-lived stateless access tokens plus long-lived server-side refresh sessions. Every refresh rotates the pair; replaying an old token wipes all of the user's sessions.
- **OTP**: 6-digit codes, hashed at rest, 10-minute expiry, per-flow attempt counters with lockouts. OpenAuth generates and verifies codes but sends nothing; delivery is the developer's job.
- **Reference app**: a small runnable Express app demonstrating one wiring of the library with MongoDB/Mongoose. Not part of the published package.

## Adapters

Documented adapters, and only these:

- Prisma (PostgreSQL): [Prisma](/docs/adapters/prisma)
- Mongoose (MongoDB): [Mongoose](/docs/adapters/mongoose)

## Documentation

Getting started:

- [Introduction](/docs): what OpenAuth is and how it is organized
- [Installation](/docs/installation): `npm install openauth`, adapter peers, reference-app setup
- [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart): register, verify, log in, and call an authenticated endpoint

Core concepts:

- [Architecture](/docs/concepts/architecture): layers, request lifecycle, adapter boundary
- [Authentication & sessions](/docs/concepts/authentication): tokens, cookies, rotation, passwords, OTP
- [Adapters](/docs/concepts/adapters): the adapter contract and record shapes
- [Validation & errors](/docs/concepts/validation-errors): Zod boundary validation, errors, status codes
- [Security](/docs/concepts/security): implemented protections and known concerns

API reference (reference-app endpoints under `/api/auth`):

- [Overview](/docs/api): conventions for auth, rate limits, validation, responses
- [GET / (status)](/docs/api/status), [POST /register](/docs/api/register), [POST /login](/docs/api/login), [POST /verify-email](/docs/api/verify-email), [POST /resend-otp](/docs/api/resend-otp), [POST /refresh](/docs/api/refresh), [GET /me](/docs/api/me), [POST /forgot-password](/docs/api/forgot-password), [POST /reset-password](/docs/api/reset-password), [POST /change-password](/docs/api/change-password), [POST /logout](/docs/api/logout)

Adapters:

- [Overview](/docs/adapters): choosing a store
- [Mongoose](/docs/adapters/mongoose): connection, models, queries
- [Prisma](/docs/adapters/prisma): schema, usage, limits

Guides:

- [Email delivery](/docs/guides/email-delivery): connecting an email provider to OTP issuance
- [Going to production](/docs/guides/production): checklist and explicit unknowns

Also on this site: [FAQ](/faq) and the [landing page](/).

## Notes

- OpenAuth is early-stage software; verify current status in the docs before building on it.
- Only behavior documented above and in the linked pages is claimed. Adapter support is exactly Prisma and Mongoose.
